recentItems.title: RiffTrax: Demonwarp (Trailer)
recentItems.description:
Get the riff: https://rifftrax.com/demonwarp

A peaceful weekend in a cabin in the woods is interrupted when a lumbering, grunting, brute of a creature arrives. And then right after George Kennedy shows up, he gets attacked by Bigfoot!

Yes, some sort of Ape Type Thing is roaming the forest ripping off both electronic equipment and heads. What does a sasquatch want with a vintage tube amp? Do cryptids possess the same tendencies as humans where they hit their forties and all of a sudden need to drop five figures on a stereo system to appreciate the production on Aja?

Look, we could tell you why he wants it, but A) it sounds so preposterous that you’d just think we made it up and B) we’ve seen it a dozen times and are still not certain it’s real. There’s a decent chance someone just spliced a different movie onto the last fifteen minutes of this one. Or maybe they passed the script around The Naked Clone style and the last person just decided to go off the rails.

If your Bigfoot/George Kennedy movie is gonna go off the rails, who better to have with you than Mike, Kevin, and Bill!

recentItems.title: RiffTrax: Return to Boggy Creek (Trailer)
recentItems.description:
Own the full riff: https://www.rifftrax.com/return-to-boggy-creek 

It’s time for the Boggy Creek Cinematic Universe to expand with Return to Boggy Creek! You wouldn’t think a rich film series could be built out of a swampy waterway in Arkansas and some kind of out-of-focus sasquatch guy, and you’d be right!

It began in 1972 with The Legend of Boggy Creek, a “docudrama” (i.e., it’s all made up) about the creature. America immediately caught Boggy Fever (unrelated to the film, just an itchy marsh-based disease) — so naturally a few years later Return to Boggy Creek, this completely unauthorized and unofficial sequel, hit theaters. The original writer and director were so inspired by that, they released an “official” sequel, Boggy Creek II: And the Legend Continues (as seen on MST3K) a few years after that. The canon is a little confusing, kind of like the Highlander series, but with way more hicks. 

Return to Boggy Creek is a surprisingly sweet family tale, starring young Dana Plato (before her Diff’rent Strokes fame) and her mom, played by Dawn Wells (after her Gilligan’s Island fame). The young girl, driven by her unexplained hatred for classmate Renee Davis, takes her younger brothers — one of whom is named T-Fish — out on a dangerous cryptid hunting expedition in the middle of a hurricane. None of the adults around them are capable of making a good decision, so it’s up to the kids and the Skunk Ape to survive the storm while guys with names like Crawfish Charlie get their heads stuck in moonshine jars, and other things of that nature. 

What is “catfish kool-aid”? You’ll want to find out, so hop in a canoe and get boggy as hell with Mike, Kevin, and Bill as they Return to Boggy Creek!

recentItems.title: RiffTrax: Monster From Green Hell (Trailer)
recentItems.description:
Get the full riff:https://www.rifftrax.com/monster-from-green-hell

A monster is terrorizing Africa. It’s a pretty big continent, but that’s about as specific as you’ll get, we’re afraid. The monster is from a region known as Green Hell, but as The Guy From Harlem taught us, that’s just where it is from. He could presently be anywhere. And where he is is: Africa.

Fortunately, there are some American scientists who are uniquely qualified to handle this situation. You see, they have shot a guinea pig and some sort of crab into space. So when Africa comes calling, they pack up their high tech gear (we dunno, Crab Rockets or something) and head to the precise location of Africa to start fighting monsters.

This involves quite a bit of walking. Turns out when all you get is a telegram saying “Trouble in Green Hell, meet up in Africa” there’s still a bit of ground to cover once you get there. The scientists come up with a brilliant idea to address this, namely “passing out and letting other people carry them.” Hey, once you’ve also shot a medium-sized rodent into space, you can criticize their methods!

We’re told the monster is a giant wasp. It bears no resemblance to a traditional wasp, but maybe it’s like one of those red pandas. Look, again, we’ve never operated a Crab Rocket. But the true message of the movie is that it turns out the wasps were not the real monster. This isn’t some crap like “the real monster was us all along,” no the real monster is the horrible buzzing sound effect that plays any time the monster is within forty miles of the main characters. It is enough to drive you mad. Maybe that’s why those crabs volunteered to go to space.

Book your ticket to Africa and join Mike, Kevin, and Bill in warding off the Monster From Green Hell!
